title: Dooars trip cost from Kolkata, line by line
meta_description: What a 3-night Dooars trip from Kolkata costs in 2026: train vs flight, rooms, safaris, car hire and food, for a couple and a family of four.
summary: A 3-night Dooars trip from Kolkata costs about ₹9,000–12,000 per person on a frugal plan with the overnight train, ₹18,000–25,000 with a private car and a mid-range resort, and ₹35,000 or more if you fly and stay premium. The train, the room and how many people share the car and jeep decide the bill.

sections.heading: The short answer
paras: Kolkata is the Dooars' biggest market, and the question we hear most is simply: how much? The answer depends less on which parks you visit than on three choices. Do you take the train or fly? Do you share a car and safari jeep with others or keep them to yourselves? And do you travel in an ordinary week or a holiday week? Here is a 3-night trip, Lataguri and Jaldapara, per person, twin sharing, including travel from Kolkata and back. All figures are indicative for 2026.

The frugal plan uses sleeper class on the Kanchankanya Express, government or family lodges, buses and autos between bases, and shared safari seats. The comfortable plan uses 3AC, a private car in the Dooars and a mid-range resort. The premium plan flies to Bagdogra and stays in the best resorts with private jeeps.

sections.heading: Train or flight
paras: For most Kolkata travellers, the train wins. The Kanchankanya Express leaves Sealdah in the evening and runs overnight through New Mal Junction, Chalsa and Hasimara to Alipurduar, so you step off near the parks in the morning without paying for a hotel night or a road transfer from Siliguri. Sleeper fares are about ₹400–550 each way and 3AC about ₹1,100–1,500, indicative 2026. Overnight trains to NJP, such as the Darjeeling Mail and Padatik Express, add a 2–3 hour road or rail leg.

Flying to Bagdogra takes about an hour, and fares range widely, from about ₹4,000 one way if booked early to well over ₹8,000 near holidays. Add a car from Bagdogra to Lataguri at ₹3,000–4,000. Flights save time but rarely money, unless you are only two people booking early. Timetables and fares change, so check current status before you travel.

Book the train as soon as the reservation window opens, which is typically about two months ahead for most Indian Railways trains, especially for Puja, Christmas and the May school holidays, when waiting lists on the Dooars trains run long. If you cannot get a confirmed berth on the Kanchankanya Express, a confirmed berth to NJP plus a local train or bus onward is better than travelling on a waitlisted ticket. Check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Rooms: the second-biggest line
paras: Rooms vary more than any other cost. At Lataguri, family-run lodges cost ₹1,200–2,500 a night; mid-range resorts such as The Reserve Gorumara cost about ₹4,500–8,000; and Sinclairs Retreat Dooars at Chalsa costs about ₹7,000–13,000. Government lodges such as Murti Banani and Aranya at Madarihat sit in between, from about ₹1,500 to ₹6,000. These are per room per night, indicative 2026, so a couple halves them per head.

Rates jump in Puja week and from 24 December to 1 January, often to double, and rise on every long weekend. Mid-week stays in November, February and March are typically 20–40% cheaper than weekends. If your dates are flexible, move them before you move hotels.

sections.heading: Cars and safaris: share and save
paras: A car for a day of Dooars sightseeing costs ₹2,500–3,500, and a transfer from Lataguri to Madarihat about ₹2,500–3,500, indicative 2026. A couple alone carries the full cost; a family of four splits it four ways. The same logic applies to safaris, which are priced per jeep for up to six people. A Gorumara jeep with a watchtower costs ₹2,500–3,500 and a Jaldapara jeep ₹2,800–4,000.

The cheapest way for a couple is to ride trains, buses and autos between bases and take shared safari seats, which lodges and counters arrange. The cheapest way for a group of five or six is often one car for the whole trip and one jeep per safari, which works out at a few hundred rupees per head for each.
list: Gorumara jeep with watchtower: ₹2,500–3,500 per jeep, up to six
Jaldapara jeep safari: ₹2,800–4,000 per jeep, up to six
Watchtower ticket only: ₹70–250 per person, plus transport
Bus or shared vehicle Siliguri–Lataguri: ₹100–200 a seat

sections.heading: A family of four, worked out
paras: Take two adults and two children aged 8 and 12, on a 3-night trip to Lataguri and Madarihat in February, travelling 3AC on the Kanchankanya Express. Train fares come to about ₹9,000–11,000 return for four. Two nights in a Lataguri mid-range room and one at Aranya, with an extra mattress, cost about ₹14,000–18,000. A car for transfers and one sightseeing day costs ₹9,000–11,000. Two safaris in a jeep for the family cost ₹5,500–7,500. Food comes to ₹6,000–8,000.

That adds up to about ₹44,000–56,000 for the family, or ₹11,000–14,000 per head, indicative 2026. Switch to sleeper class and a family lodge and it falls to about ₹30,000–36,000. Travel in Puja week and it can pass ₹70,000. Children under 5 usually stay free in parents' rooms, and many lodges charge a small fee for an extra mattress rather than a second room.

sections.heading: A couple on a frugal plan, worked out
paras: Now take two friends or a couple on the cheapest sensible version of the same trip in late November. Sleeper class on the Kanchankanya Express costs about ₹1,000 each for the return journey. Two nights in a Lataguri family lodge at ₹1,500 a room and one night in a simple Madarihat hotel at ₹1,800 come to about ₹2,400 each. Autos, a bus to Madarihat and the auto to Hasimara station add about ₹600 each.

Two safaris in shared jeeps, one Gorumara watchtower and one Jaldapara dawn safari, cost about ₹1,000–1,300 each when six people fill the jeep. Meals at roadside hotels and lodges run about ₹1,500 each for the three days, and extras such as camera fees, tea and a dance programme about ₹800. The total is about ₹7,300–7,600 per person, indicative 2026. That is less than the price of one return flight to Bagdogra in a busy week, for a trip that sees the same animals.

sections.heading: Where the bill creeps up
paras: Small costs add up in the Dooars. Camera fees and guide fees are charged at some parks on top of the safari. Evening cultural programmes at lodges cost ₹100–300 a head. Elephant rides, where offered, cost ₹1,000–2,000 per person. Lunches at resorts on safari days, mineral water, and tips for drivers and guides each add a few hundred rupees a day. Build in ₹500–1,000 per person per day for these.

The biggest hidden cost is a missed safari. If you arrive without a booking in peak season, you may end up paying a tout double or not getting in at all. Book safaris online on the official system the day slots open.

sections.heading: Five ways to cut 20 percent
paras: None of these makes the trip worse. Most of them make it calmer.
list: Travel Sunday to Wednesday instead of over the weekend.
Take the overnight train and skip a hotel night.
Share safari jeeps with other travellers to fill all six seats.
Stay in government lodges or family-run Lataguri lodges instead of resorts.
Pick one base per park and avoid paying a car to sit idle.

faqs.q: How much does a Dooars trip from Kolkata cost
faqs.a: A 3-night trip to Lataguri and Jaldapara costs about ₹9,000–12,000 per person on a frugal plan with sleeper class and shared safaris, ₹18,000–25,000 with 3AC, a private car and a mid-range resort, and ₹35,000 or more if you fly and stay premium, twin sharing, indicative 2026. Holiday weeks cost more.

faqs.q: Which train is best from Kolkata to the Dooars
faqs.a: The Kanchankanya Express from Sealdah, because it runs overnight right through the Dooars, stopping at New Mal Junction for Lataguri and Hasimara for Jaldapara. Trains to NJP, such as the Darjeeling Mail and Padatik Express, also work but need a 2–3 hour onward leg. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is it cheaper to fly or take the train to the Dooars
faqs.a: The train is almost always cheaper: sleeper costs about ₹400–550 one way and 3AC about ₹1,100–1,500, indicative 2026, and saves a hotel night. Flights to Bagdogra start around ₹4,000 one way if booked early, plus a ₹3,000–4,000 car to Lataguri. Flying saves time, not money.

faqs.q: How much is a Dooars trip for a family of four
faqs.a: For two adults and two school-age children, 3 nights by 3AC with a mid-range room, a car and two family safaris cost about ₹44,000–56,000 in total, indicative 2026. With sleeper class and a family lodge, about ₹30,000–36,000. Puja week can push it past ₹70,000.

faqs.q: Are Dooars prices higher during Durga Puja
faqs.a: Yes, sharply. Puja week is the most expensive week of the year in the Dooars, with room rates often doubling, trains full and safari seats selling out on release. The Christmas and New Year week is next. If you must travel then, book rooms and trains months ahead and safaris as soon as booking opens.

faqs.q: Do safari prices include entry fees
faqs.a: Usually the safari ticket covers the vehicle, the route and the entry, while guide fees and camera charges may be added at the counter. It varies by park and season. Ask when you book and carry some cash for extras. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How much should I budget for extras
faqs.a: Allow ₹500–1,000 per person per day for camera fees, guide fees, evening dance programmes, mineral water, snacks and tips. Elephant rides, where offered, cost ₹1,000–2,000 per person on top, indicative 2026. Shopping for tea or local crafts is extra again.

faqs.q: Is 3 nights enough for a Dooars trip from Kolkata
faqs.a: Three nights covers Gorumara and Jaldapara with one or two safaris each, which is what most families want. With 4–5 nights you can add Jhalong, Samsing or Buxa and Jayanti at a slower pace. Two nights is enough for Gorumara alone.

faqs.q: Can I pay by UPI in the Dooars
faqs.a: UPI works at most shops, hotels and restaurants in Lataguri, Malbazar and Madarihat. Forest lodges, autos, village homestays and some safari extras may want cash, and mobile data can drop in the forests. Carry ₹2,000–3,000 in cash per person. ATMs are available at Malbazar, Madarihat and Hasimara.
